Infelizmente eu não tenho exemplos com florestas plantadas. Eu tenho exemplos com batatas disponíveis aqui: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P7

2) https://groups.google.com/g/fieldimager/c/V8T5VsLAP5U/m/oHVP-0TVEgAJ

Outra sugestão seria tentar pegar imagens pelo Google Earth. Geralmente funciona bem. Veja algum exemplo de floresta plantada perto da sua região ou com a mesma especie que voce ira trabalhar.

Vamos ver se alguém aqui da comunidade nos ajuda compartilhando um exemplo (o pipeline funciona para tif e jpg).

Tenha um excelente ano,
Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,
I change the function fieldMask and upgrade the package to version 0.2.6.
Please try to upgrade the version and follow the code below:

devtools::install_github("filipematias23/FIELDimageR") #0.2.6
library(FIELDimageR)
library(raster)
EX1<-stack("flir_20210104T131612_fullVIS.jpg")
EX2<-stack("flir_20210104T131612.jpg")

EX1.RemSoil<-fieldMask(mosaic = EX1, Red = 1, Green = 2, Blue = 3,
                       index = "BGI", cropValue = 1.1, cropAbove = T)                #removing background in visible image

EX1.RemSoil<-fieldMask(mosaic = EX2,mask = EX1.RemSoil$mask, projection = F)

All the best,
Filipe

This is what I'm using.
# Estimating plant height
# Uploading files from soil base (EX_DSM0.tif) and vegetative growth (EX_DSM1.tif):
DSM0 <- stack("DSM0 HIYT 3-23.tif")
DSM1 <- stack("DSM1 HIYT 6-11.tif")

# Cropping the image using the previous shape from step 2:
DSM0.C <- fieldCrop(mosaic = DSM0,fieldShape = EX1.Crop)
DSM1.C <- fieldCrop(mosaic = DSM1,fieldShape = EX1.Crop)

# Canopy Height Model (CHM):
DSM0.R <- resample(DSM0.C, DSM1.C)
CHM <- DSM1.C-DSM0.R
plot(CHM)

# Rotating the image using the same theta from step 3:
CHM.R<-fieldRotate(CHM, theta = -0.979)

# Removing the soil using mask from step 4:
CHM.S <- fieldMask(CHM.R, mask = EX1.RemSoil$mask)

# Extracting the estimate plant height average (EPH):
EPH <- fieldInfo(CHM.S$newMosaic, fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape, fun = "mean")

EPH$plotValue

About the "table" question:

(1) If you are looking only for image data extraction, with no intention to compare the results with traits collected manually in the field (e.g., yield, maturity, etc.), the answer is YES. FIELDimageR can make the table by itself. The data ID (PlotName) will be organized from left to right and top to bottom (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P5).

(2) However, if you want to have the same sequence or plot identification from your field and combine the image data with the traits collected manually in the field (e.g., yield, maturity, etc.), the answer is NO. In this case, you must provide a MAP (matrix object in R) with the right plot identification. Also, you need to provide a data table with one column that matches the MAP identification ID. For example, input table with (Plot, Row, Range and a sequence of field traits collected manually) like in this example: https://drive.google.com/file/d/18YE4dlSY1Czk2nKeHgwd9xBX8Yu6RCl7/view.

I tried to explain what the function fieldShape does here: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P5

Let me know if it makes sense,

Filipe

Hi Amir,

As Tej said, this is just a warning msg about the rotation. fieldRotate() changes the image geographic position to be easier to use fieldShape() and draw the field shapefile.

If you want to keep the same CRS after drawing the shapefile you can use the following strategy:

1) Using "extentGIS=TRUE" on fieldRotate():
source(system.file("extdata", "fieldRotate.R", package = "FIELDimageR"))
EX1.Rotated<-fieldRotate(mosaic = EX1.Crop, theta = 2.3, extentGIS=TRUE)

2) Followed by informing the rotation angle "theta" on fieldShape():
EX1.Shape<-fieldShape(mosaic = EX1.RemSoil, ncols = 14, nrows = 9,
                                            fieldMap = fieldMap, fieldData = DataTable, ID = "Plot",
                                            theta = 2.3)
plotRGB(EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic)
plot(EX1.Shape$fieldShape,add=T)
plotRGB(EX1)
plot(EX1.Shape$fieldShapeGIS,add=T)

All the best,
Filipe
